boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Rocky Face Ridge record (May 7-13, 1864) in Atlanta Campaign [May-September 1864]. The frozen record covers the demonstrations at Buzzard Roost (Mill Creek Gap), Dug Gap and the ridge, with the cavalry affairs near Varnell's Station; McPherson's advance through Snake Creek Gap toward Resaca on May 9 is context, and the May 13 fighting at Resaca belongs to GA008. The live NPS page labels the campaign "Morgan's Raid Into Kentucky" and dates it May-September 1864; neither field replaces the frozen campaign or battle interval. Campaign-wide totals are context and are not assigned to this record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force fields name the Military Division of the Mississippi and the Army of Tennessee without counts; the live field reads zero. Cox gives Sherman an effective force of nearly 100,000 men and 254 guns at the opening of the campaign (Cumberland 60,000, Tennessee 25,000, Ohio 14,000) and argues that Johnston's 44,000 effectives at Dalton on May 1 understate the number present; his Appendix A gives 52,990 officers and men present for duty on May 1 (the April 30 table totals 52,992). Johnston gives 40,900 effective infantry and artillery after Mercer's brigade arrived and about 4,000 effective cavalry, puts Sherman's army at the Missionary Ridge force (then 80,000) plus reinforcements and cites Wheeler's estimate of 15,000 Union cavalry. Johnston says Wheeler with 2,200 men defeated more than double that number of Union cavalry near Varnell's Station on the 12th.
claims.rationale: Army-wide figures on different bases (Union effective force; Confederate effectives, which Cox says exclude officers and men not bearing arms; present for duty) and dates; none measures the troops engaged at the ridge and none is adopted. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Cox describes the crest attacked by Newton's division as so narrow that no deployment could be made, and the Dug Gap approach as ending at a perpendicular wall with only clefts leading up through it. Johnston says Rocky Face and Snake Creek Gap at its south end completely covered the Union movement to turn Dalton. NPS says Johnston had entrenched on the ridge and across Crow Valley.
claims.rationale: Ground described by an interested history, an interested report and a summary; no map verification. The ridge and the Confederate works predated the engagement, but the works' timing is not established here, so no inherited tag is assigned.

claims.value: The frozen result is a Union victory, glossed as forcing the Confederates off the ridge; the live page reads Union Victory. Johnston says five assaults on Hood's troops on the 9th were all repulsed and that his infantry and artillery marched for Resaca on the night of the 12th. Cox says the enemy had been compelled to evacuate the Dalton lines. NPS says Johnston retired toward Resaca on the 12th after discovering Sherman's movement.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The Confederate withdrawal followed the turning movement; tactical repulses on the ridge are recorded separately.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown, while the frozen result note says Union casualties were high; the live field reads 1437 (US 837; CS 600). Cox says losses for Dalton and Resaca cannot be given accurately because the reports covered a month, puts Union killed and wounded before Dalton at not more than six or eight hundred and calls Sherman's loss trifling; he gives about 150 on each side for the cavalry affair of the 9th and some scores on each side on the 11th. The inspected Johnston report gives no Rocky Face figure.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. The cavalry figures are for separate affairs and are not added to the ridge fighting; 'high' and 'trifling' characterizations conflict.

open_questions: Sherman's, Thomas's, Howard's, Hooker's and Geary's reports, Hood's corps report on Rocky Face (read, not cited here), Hardee's itinerary, the compiled casualty returns (Nos. 600-601) and the cavalry reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cox's Atlanta (Scribner, 1882) is a second: a retrospective Union history by the Twenty-third Corps division commander, drawing on official reports and memoirs, so it is not independent of them. Johnston's October 20, 1864 report, printed in Volume XXXVIII Part 3, is a third family (interested Confederate account). Official Records Series I Volume XXXVIII is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting. Campaign-wide strength and loss totals are context, not assigned to one record.
